built.detail: What can be lawfully measured about AI compute: quarterly capital expenditure from the seven companies whose capex is the buildout, read from their own XBRL facts on SEC EDGAR, plus GPU cloud service health and verified benchmark registries.

built.detail: This section is meant to track capital flowing into AI companies by funding stage and sector.

built.detail: This section tracks cumulative AI-related patent counts for 108 companies, ranking them by total portfolio size and charting how the combined total moves over time.

built.name: Security Incidents
built.detail: This section tracks open incidents reported on the status pages of 12 AI infrastructure and model providers, including Anthropic, OpenAI, Cohere, Lambda, Fireworks AI, Baseten, Deepgram, and ElevenLabs.

title: AI Observatory
answer: Live telemetry on the health of the field: release cadence, repository activity, uptime, GPU availability, funding, patents, and regulatory movement.

reading.body:
The AI Observatory measures the field's health across eight streams, but only compute capex is tied to the physical buildout.

The telemetry splits into two kinds. Model release cadence, repository activity, Hugging Face downloads, API uptime, and security incidents are software-side signals, counted in the tens of thousands of models and dozens of providers. Compute telemetry is the exception: it reads quarterly capital expenditure from the seven companies whose capex funds the buildout, taken from their own XBRL facts on SEC EDGAR. That is the only stream here that connects AI to buildings and power, and it does so through disclosed financial facts rather than estimates.

The counts show where the field's weight sits. Model release cadence and Hugging Face trends each carry 16,356 entries, repository activity covers 55 repositories, and patent filings cover 108 companies. Uptime and security incidents each cover 12 providers, and compute telemetry covers 11 entities. Funding activity is listed as intended rather than built, so capital flowing into AI companies by stage and sector is not yet measured here.

What this does not tell you is magnitude. The data gives coverage counts and sources, not the values themselves: no capex figures, no uptime percentages, no download totals, no incident durations. It also does not cover power procurement, grid interconnection, or data center construction directly, so the binding constraint on AI scaling is only visible here through the capex of seven companies, and only at quarterly resolution.
